chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A contracted slave bought himself, and left wealth valued at one hundred thousand, and he had no inheritor.' He said: 'The one who is the guardian of his actions will inherit him.' I said, 'Who is the guarantor of his actions?' He said: 'The guarantor of the actions of the Muslims.'

key_terms.الضَّامِنُ: The guarantor or one who assumes responsibility.
key_terms.جَرِيرَةٌ: Action, deed, or liability; here referring to the responsibility for the individual's affairs.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٌ: A slave who has entered into a contract to buy his freedom by paying a sum to his master.

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a contracted slave who dies with no other heirs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a mukatab dying without heirs passes his estate to the 'guarantor of the Muslims' (Dhamin al-Jara'ir), a title the Imam identifies as the Imam himself. This ruling underscores the Imam's role as the ultimate heir and legal successor in the absence of familial ties, reinforcing the concept of divine guardianship (Wilayah) over the community's assets. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the financial authority of the Imam in Shia jurisprudence.
